answer: Each agent earns a reputation token that ripples through the network when it finishes a verified task, incrementally anchoring its identity to a time‑stamped ledger. Tokens decay during inactivity, so a Sybil attacker must continuously fund every fake node with fresh proofs, turning idle time into a cost sink. The expense grows like a comet’s tail: the longer the fake swarm lives, the exponentially higher the staking and compute required.
